newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Israeli envoy says Hamas linked to Argentine blast.
newsitem.headline: Israeli envoy says Hamas linked to Argentine blast.

text.p: Israel's U.N. envoy cited a statement on Friday by a leader of the Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement as implying responsibility for the 1992 bombing of Israel's embassy in Buenos Aires that killed 29 people and wounded more than 200.

Ambassador David Peleg was commenting on a letter he sent to U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan giving details of the suicide bombing of a Tel Aviv cafe earlier on Friday that killed four people, including the bomber, and injured more than 40.

The letter quoted from a speech that Peleg said was delivered on Friday in Khan Younis, in the Gaza Strip, by the chief of Hamas's military wing, Ibrahim al-Makadmeh, who was released from prison recently by the Palestinian self-rule authority.
Makadmeh was quoted as saying: "We should not have mercy on our enemies; our people have an obligation to chase them, whether they live in Tel Aviv or in Latin America."
Peleg told reporters this reference to Latin America, and the proximity to the March 17 date in 1992 when Israel's embassy in Buenos Aires was bombed, "speak for themselves."
No one has yet been charged with that bombing, though Israel has in the past blamed Iranian-backed fundamentalists.
